profile_basis: Based on direct inspection of the FULL bundled GitHub corpus (26,637 records scanned) plus the benchmark harness source code. This is a stronger evidentiary basis than the mission anticipated (README/code-only, no data); values below are marked CONFIRMED where derived from the actual full-corpus scan, and UNKNOWN/README-claimed where not independently verified.

memory_retrieval.basis: Every record's transcript (message_list) is the memory substrate to be stored, and QA.target_step_id gives a gold evidence pointer confirming retrieval is a well-defined, scoreable operation (harness's own get_recall() in benchmark/env/Membenenv.py implements this exact comparison).

test_time_learning.basis: No source-provided mechanism or annotation for in-context/test-time learning beyond ordinary memory storage; the harness stores each turn and answers a downstream question, but there is no explicit 'learning update' signal distinct from memory writes.

long_range_understanding.basis: Trajectories run to many sessions/turns (RecMultiSession, highlevel_rec categories) with a question posed only after the full trajectory; the 'noisy'/MakeNoise mechanism is explicitly designed to extend context length further, confirming long-range understanding is a first-class evaluated capability.

conflict_resolution.basis: The knowledge_update category (confirmed present, both variants, 999 records total) is designed around fact changes over time, which implies conflict/update scenarios per its name and the README's category description, but no explicit 'conflicting-fact pair' annotation field was found on the records themselves beyond the ordinary transcript + QA structure -- conflict handling must be inferred from transcript content, not read off a dedicated field.

knowledge_update.basis: Dedicated knowledge_update.json files exist for both FirstAgent and ThirdAgent (999 records total, confirmed by full scan), matching the mission's named category exactly.

noise_robustness.basis: Dedicated noisy.json category files (confirmed present, both variants, 3178 records total by scan) plus a separate, reusable noise-injection pipeline (MakeNoise/NoiseMeta/{messagenoise_new,sessionnoise_new}.json, 46MB/13MB pools of distractor dialogue) confirmed bundled and inspected -- this is a deliberately engineered capability, not incidental noise.

multi_session_memory.basis: RecMultiSession.json (FirstAgent, multi_agent scenario, 500 records) is explicitly multi-session by name and structure; the nested message_list container shape (list of sessions, each a list of turns) used across most FirstAgent categories also structurally supports multi-session grouping.

agentic_task_memory.basis: MemBench's task is conversational QA over remembered facts/preferences/events, not agentic tool-use or task-execution memory; no tool-call or task-execution trace fields were found in any record.

evidence_availability.basis: QA.target_step_id present on 26,633/26,637 records (99.985%, full-corpus scan), pointing to specific transcript turn location(s) via [session_index, turn_index] pairs.

answer_availability.basis: QA.answer (free text) and QA.ground_truth (MC letter) present on 26,637/26,637 records (100%, full-corpus scan).

memory_ids.basis: tid is a source-native, per-scenario-unique record identifier (confirmed 0 duplicates across the full scan); turn-level ids (sid/mid) are also present, letting individual memory units be addressed.

stable_ids.basis: tid is stable and unique (confirmed). qid is NOT reliably unique (duplicated in ~99% of records per scenario, confirmed by scan) -- callers must not treat qid alone as a stable identifier.

provenance.basis: Each record documents its own generation category/scenario/variant (a form of structural provenance), and rel/attr/value triples on fact-establishing turns document which fact a turn encodes -- but there is no explicit generation-pipeline metadata (e.g. model version, prompt template id, generation timestamp) attached to individual records.

lineage.basis: No parent/child or derivation relationship between records was found anywhere in the corpus.

equivalence.basis: No cross-record equivalence annotation (e.g. two records marked as testing the same underlying fact) was found.

temporal_order.basis: Every turn carries an explicit time field (e.g. "'2024-10-01 08:00' Tuesday") and QA.time gives the question's reference time; turns within a session/trajectory are also implicitly ordered by sid/mid.

task_records.basis: Each tid groups a coherent task instance (a transcript + one QA pair), confirmed structurally consistent (0 malformed) across the full scan.

agent_visible_context.basis: Constructible directly from message_list + QA.question/time/choices; verified against phase3/evaluation/contracts/boundary.py with 0 forbidden-key violations across all 275 normalized sample records.

evaluator_reference.basis: Constructible directly from QA.answer/ground_truth/target_step_id; cleanly separable from agent_visible_context (verified, see above).

data_gap_caveat: All AVAILABLE/PARTIAL values above are based on a full scan of the actual GitHub-bundled corpus (26,637 records), not merely README claims -- this is a stronger basis than a typical Drive/Baidu-unavailable scenario would allow. The two values still marked NOT_PROVIDED_BY_SOURCE (lineage, equivalence, test_time_learning, agentic_task_memory) reflect a genuine absence in the source data itself, confirmed by inspection, not a data-access gap.
